text:
anya: quick triage — SampleProf shows a recurring tail spike when the batcher flips kernel for qwen-32 at seq > 1024. stack traces attached :thinking_face:
leo: @anya can you paste the flamegraph + the kernel selection log? my hunch is kernel churn + KV evictions. :eyes:
anya: pasted trace + counters below. note the kernel switch at 00:00:08 relative to request start, and KV cache miss rate jumps from 3% -> 27%

--- trace snippet ---
Flame: sampleprof://run/1766012345/trace1
Counters:
  batch_size=8
  seq_len=1536
  kernel_selected=matmul_opt_v2 -> fallback_loop_v1
  kv_cache_pages=12/16
  kv_miss_rate=0.27
  mem_avail=11.2GiB
  gpu_util=68%

Config used:
```
batcher:{ policy: adaptive, max_batch_tokens: 8192, switch_threshold_ms: 6 }
kernel_router:{prefer: matmul_opt_v2, fallback: fallback_loop_v1}
kv_cache:{format: fp8_packed, eviction: lru_pages}
```
--- end ---

ram: that fp8_packed KV representation has a known issue with page-alignment on 32-head layouts. If kernel A expects contiguous kv strides and kernel B reads with different alignment, it ends up copying + reallocating pages -> eviction churn.
marta: i repro'd locally by toggling kernel routing. forcing `kernel_router.prefer=fallback_loop_v1` removed the churn but added 15% cpu overhead on host. latency tail dropped ~22%.
leo: did you try switching KV format to fp16 to avoid misaligned packing? how much memory delta?
anya: yes — fp16 cache (same pages) increased resident by ~18% but reduced eviction rate to 4% and tail p99 down from 310ms -> 240ms. throughput stable. token cost up slightly.
ram: alternative is hybrid layout: keep fp8 packed for cold pages, promote hot prefixes to fp16 pinned pages. that would require hotset tracking + async promotion. overhead: a small GC loop and a promote RPC.
leo: can we short-circuit kernel switch while promoting? idea: if batcher detects kernel switch for a request that touches promoted prefixes, hold the switch for up to 2ms to allow async promotion finish. reduces kernel churn.
marta: implemented locally — adding a 2ms hold reduced p99 by another 10% on my runs. code diff is tiny:
```
if (kernel_change && touches_promoted_prefixes) {
  sleep(2ms);
  recompute_kernel_decision();
}
```
leo: nice. risks: increases tail when promotion never completes, so need a fallback timeout and metrics.
anya: infra-bot scheduled an A/B to test these changes on dedicated pool-c.
infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout scheduled to pool-c at 2026-03-18T16:40:00Z for commit abc123 (batcher hold + hot-promotion) :white_check_mark:

marta: next steps I propose:
- short term: enable fp16 for prefixes by default on qwen-32 when seq>1024 (config flag)
- mid term: implement hotset tracker + async promotion (ram owns)
- monitor: add metric `kv_promotion_latency_ms` and `kernel_switch_hold_count`

leo: agree. also add a kernel-router metric for `switch_count_per_min` so we can detect churn early.
anya: tagging product/console for dashboards. will open PR with experimental flag + dashboard links. thanks all :thumbsup:
